summary: Atobe–Kondo–Yasuda define compact open subgroups K_{n,λ} of GL_n(F) indexed by tuples λ. They state local newform theory for all irreducible representations: dim π^{K_{n,λ_π}} = 1 and vanishing below λ_π (Theorems 2.1, 2.2). The proof runs through a Mackey reduction, determinantal formulas for type-χ representations, and Rankin–Selberg integrals in Shalika models for Speh representations. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed, and nineteen findings are recorded. Theorem 9.1's uniqueness is false (E1), Lemma 8.10 fails at repeated parameters (E3), and hence the paper does not establish Theorem 2.1 for Speh representations with L(s, π) = 1 and n, m ≥ 2 (E19). Not formalised.

items.name: PID torsion-module decomposition
items.statement: For a commutative domain R with IsPrincipalIdealRing R and a finitely generated torsion R-module M, there are finite indices, irreducibles p_i and natural e_i with M linearly equivalent to the direct sum of R/(p_i^e_i). This supplies existence, not uniqueness of a sorted DVR sequence.

items.name: Artinian Jacobson radical is nilpotent
items.statement: For any (not necessarily commutative) Artinian ring R, the Jacobson radical of the zero ideal is nilpotent.

items.name: Compact valuation balls
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field K and gamma in its value group with zero, {x | valuation K x <= gamma} is compact.

items.name: Smooth representation and compact fixed-space interface
items.statement: Use the SR.0 smooth complex category. For compact open K define pi^K; compact averaging of Haar mass one projects onto it and is exact over C.

api.name: SmoothRep.average_fixed
api.statement: For normalized Haar mass one, e_K(v)=v for v in pi^K and e_K squared=e_K.

api.name: SmoothRep.fixed_map
api.statement: An intertwiner f restricts to pi^K→tau^K and commutes with e_K; restrictions preserve identity and composition.

api.name: SmoothRep.fixed_exact
api.statement: A short exact sequence of smooth complex representations gives a short exact sequence of compact-open K-fixed spaces.

uses.how: pass fixed vectors through exact sequences and conjugacy.

items.name: Normalized parabolic induction and Jacquet modules
items.statement: For an ordered partition of n, pi_1×...×pi_r denotes normalized smooth induction from the corresponding standard parabolic, with modulus square root over C; use normalized Jacquet restriction.

api.name: SmoothRep.induced_eval
api.statement: A normalized induced section obeys f(pg)=delta_P(p)^(1/2) pi_L(p)f(g).

api.name: SmoothRep.induced_map
api.statement: A tensor product of Levi intertwiners induces a G-intertwiner, respecting identity and composition.

api.name: SmoothRep.induction_transitive
api.statement: For nested standard parabolics, normalized induction in stages agrees with direct induction, with delta_P=delta_Q times the Levi modulus.

uses.how: convert compact invariants and Levi restrictions into tensor products with the correct modulus.

items.name: Iterated highest derivative
items.statement: For pi irreducible, start pi^(0)=pi and iterate its nonzero derivative of greatest order; continue by G_0. Each highest derivative is irreducible in the GL_n setting.
items.note: Requires an early complex specialization of SR.5, not dependence on its late integral-family or spectral outputs.

api.name: SmoothRep.highestDerivative_order
api.statement: Record the greatest ordinary derivative order r with pi^(r) nonzero and the resulting GL_(n-r) representation.

api.name: SmoothRep.highestDerivative_iterate
api.statement: The zeroth iterate is pi, the successor is the highest derivative of the preceding iterate, and G_0 remains G_0.

api.name: SmoothRep.highestDerivative_segment
api.statement: For Z(m), the highest derivative is Z(m^-), losing sum of the cuspidal degrees of all segments.

uses.how: iterate highest derivatives while distinguishing ordinary derivative order.

items.name: Analytic conductor exponent
items.statement: c_pi is the nonnegative integer characterized by epsilon(s,pi,psi)=epsilon(0,pi,psi) q^(-c_pi s), with psi of conductor o; conductor of G_0 is zero.

api.name: LocalFactor.conductor_spec
api.statement: For conductor-o psi, epsilon(s,pi,psi)=epsilon(0,pi,psi)q^(-c_pi s), with unique c_pi in N.

api.name: LocalFactor.conductor_unramifiedTwist
api.statement: Twisting pi by an unramified character preserves c_pi, although the epsilon scalar can change.

api.name: LocalFactor.conductor_induction
api.statement: For irreducible normalized pi_1×...×pi_r, the conductor is the sum of the conductors of its factors.

uses.how: extract integral exponents and unramified twist behavior.

items.name: Cuspidal segments and linkedness
items.statement: A nonempty segment [a,b]_rho has a,b real with b-a a nonnegative integer, rho irreducible cuspidal on G_d,d>=1. Equivalent cuspidal twisting presentations are identified. Linked segments have union a segment and neither contains the other; precedence uses the source order. On a fixed type-chi line use integral endpoints.

api.name: Segment.rank
api.statement: The GL rank of [a,b]_rho is degree(rho)(b-a+1), while its interval length is b-a+1.

api.name: Segment.linked_iff
api.statement: On the same cuspidal line, after ordering left endpoints a<c, linkedness is a<c<=b+1 and b<d.

api.name: Segment.elementaryOperation
api.statement: For a linked pair replace it by its union and its intersection, omitting an empty intersection; cuspidal support and total rank are preserved.

uses.how: classify constituents and perform elementary operations.

items.name: Multisegments and Zelevinsky classification
items.statement: A multisegment is a finite multiset of segments; Z(m) is the unique irreducible subobject of a product ordered so that earlier segments do not precede later ones. This gives all irreducibles of GL_n with total GL rank n; L(m) is the Langlands-quotient convention and m# satisfies L(m)=Z(m#).

api.name: Multisegment.induction_order_independent
api.statement: The allowed Zelevinsky ordered product has the same irreducible subobject up to isomorphism for every allowed ordering.

api.name: Multisegment.rank_add
api.statement: Total rank is additive in the finite multiset sum, counting segment multiplicities and cuspidal degrees.

api.name: Multisegment.dual_involutive
api.statement: The Zelevinsky multisegment dual preserves cuspidal support and has (m#)#=m.

uses.how: preserve multiplicities under classification and duality.

items.name: Derivative conductor tuple
items.statement: For pi on G_n define lambda_pi,k=c_(pi^(n-k))-c_(pi^(n-k+1)), 1<=k<=n. Its membership in Lambda_n is a theorem, not a constructor assumption.

api.name: Newform.conductorTuple_apply
api.statement: The kth component is c_(pi^(n-k))-c_(pi^(n-k+1)), with the highest-derivative iteration convention.

api.name: Newform.conductorTuple_sum
api.statement: The sum of the n components telescopes to c_pi, since the nth iterate is G_0 of conductor0.

api.name: Newform.conductorTuple_mem
api.statement: Using Proposition2.4, the components are nonnegative and weakly increasing.

uses.how: relate lex minimality and conductor weight.

items.name: Row-depth compact groups
items.statement: For lambda in Lambda_n, K_n,lambda={k in GL_n(o) | k_ij-delta_ij in p^lambda_i for every i,j}; Lambda_n, its lex order, weight and padded addition are part of this interface.

api.name: Newform.rowLevel_mem
api.statement: k is in K_n,lambda iff k is in GL_n(o) and each row i differs from identity by entries in p^lambda_i.

api.name: Newform.rowLevel_antitone
api.statement: If lambda_i<=mu_i for every i then K_n,mu is a subgroup of K_n,lambda; lex order alone does not imply this inclusion.

api.name: Newform.rowLevel_compactOpen
api.statement: K_n,lambda is a compact open subgroup, containing the principal congruence kernel of depth max_i lambda_i.

uses.how: manipulate row congruences and padded tuple order.

items.name: Newform line and nonzero vectors
items.statement: A local newform of pi is any nonzero vector in pi^(K_n,lambda_pi). The line is canonical, but no canonical nonzero basis is asserted.

api.name: Newform.mem_iff
api.statement: v is a newform iff v is nonzero and every k in K_n,lambda_pi fixes v.

api.name: Newform.map_equiv
api.statement: An isomorphism of representations carries the newform subspace and its nonzero vectors bijectively to those of the target.

api.name: Newform.normalized_unique
api.statement: Conditional on dimension one and a functional ell nonzero on the line, there is a unique newform v with ell(v)=1.

uses.how: use a line without choosing an unjustified canonical vector.

items.name: Newform multiplicity one
items.statement: For every pi in Irr(G_n), dim_C pi^(K_n,lambda_pi)=1. This is the printed target; its proof closure is conditional on resolving the §9 separation defect.
items.note: OPEN proof obligation; do not mark formalized or use the false uniqueness theorem as an axiom. (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026) The paper's gap for this case is recorded as E19.

items.name: Lexicographic vanishing
items.statement: For pi in Irr(G_n) and lambda in Lambda_n with lambda<lambda_pi in lex order, pi^(K_n,lambda)=0. The §9-dependent branch remains unclosed.
items.note: (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026) The paper's gap for this case is recorded as E19.

items.name: Conductor-weight vanishing
items.statement: For pi in Irr(G_n), if lambda in Lambda_n has sum(lambda_i)<c_pi=sum(lambda_pi,i), then pi^(K_n,lambda)=0. This criterion is separate from lex vanishing.

items.name: Conductor as minimal level weight
items.statement: Conditional on the main existence/vanishing statements, c_pi=min{|lambda| : pi^(K_n,lambda) is nonzero}.

items.name: Right truncation and ram operation
items.statement: Delta^-=[a,b-1]_rho with empty intervals removed; m^- is the multiset sum. On unipotent m put m^ram=((m#)^-)#. A type-chi line has chi unramified and integer twists.

api.name: Multisegment.truncate_add
api.statement: Right truncation distributes over multiset sum and sends [a,a] to the empty multiset.

api.name: Multisegment.ram_def
api.statement: For unipotent m, ram(m)=dual(truncate(dual(m))); no additivity for arbitrary sums is asserted.

api.name: Multisegment.truncate_rank
api.statement: rank(m^-)=rank(m)-sum_Delta degree(rho_Delta).

uses.how: relate images and derivative ranks.

items.name: Multisegment conductor tuple
items.statement: For nonunipotent segments Delta_i=[a_i,b_i]_rho_i sum the left-zero-padded tails c_rho_i repeated length(Delta_i). For unipotent m sum left-zero-padded tails of ones of lengths of the segments in m^ram. Split a general m into its unipotent and other parts and add.

api.name: Multisegment.conductorTuple_tail
api.statement: A nonunipotent segment of length l contributes a padded length-l tail of c_rho.

api.name: Multisegment.conductorTuple_unipotent
api.statement: For unipotent m, component k counts the ram-segments with length at least n-k+1.

api.name: Multisegment.conductorTuple_split
api.statement: Splitting off the complete unipotent part gives the sum of its tuple and the tuple of the remaining nonunipotent part after common padding.

uses.how: compute the target tuple without repeated analytic conductors.

items.name: Derivative and multisegment tuples agree
items.statement: For pi=Z(m) of rank n>=1, lambda_pi=lambda_m; in particular the derivative differences are ascending nonnegative integers.

items.name: Generic specialization
items.statement: For generic irreducible pi, lambda_pi=(0^(n-1),c_pi), and the groups/newform claim specialize to the JPSS generic theorem.

items.name: Ladder multisegments
items.statement: A type-chi multisegment [x_1,y_1]+...+[x_t,y_t] is ladder when x_1>...>x_t and y_1>...>y_t; chi is unramified here.

api.name: Multisegment.isLadder_iff
api.statement: A presentation is ladder iff left endpoints and right endpoints are each strictly decreasing along the same list.

api.name: Multisegment.ladder_ram
api.statement: For unramified chi, ladder ram is the multiset [x_(i-1)-1,y_i] for i=2..t, omitting empty intervals.

api.name: Multisegment.ladder_capacity
api.statement: For permutation w the ith determinant capacity is y_i-x_(w(i))+1; zero means G_0 and negative means zero contribution.

uses.how: use adjacent overlap lengths and determinant capacities.

items.name: Explicit ladder tuple
items.statement: For a type-chi ladder [x_1,y_1]+...+[x_t,y_t] in decreasing endpoint order, lambda_pi is the SUM, for i=2,...,t, of the n-tuples with max(y_i-x_(i-1)+2,0) terminal ones and all other entries zero. These lengths are not themselves the coordinates of lambda.

items.name: Irreducible-product tuple addition
items.statement: If each pi_i is either in the L(s,pi_i)=1 class of Example2.5(1) or is a type-chi ladder of Example2.5(2), and pi_1×...×pi_r is irreducible, then lambda of the product is the sum of the lambda_pi_i after left-zero-padding.

items.name: Tempered Speh representation
items.statement: For irreducible tempered pi of G_n and m>=1, Sp(pi,m) is the unique irreducible subrepresentation of pi|.|^(-(m-1)/2) × ... × pi|.|^((m-1)/2).

api.name: Speh.of_tempered
api.statement: For m>=1 and irreducible tempered pi, construct the unique irreducible subrepresentation of the ascending normalized twist product in the source.

api.name: Speh.dual
api.statement: The smooth contragredient of Sp(pi,m) is isomorphic to Sp(dual pi,m).

api.name: Speh.conductorTuple
api.statement: The conductor tuple of Sp(pi,m) has (n-1)m leading zeros and m copies of c_pi.

uses.how: pass between models and compute levels.

items.name: Speh conductor tuple
items.statement: For sigma=Sp(pi,m), lambda_sigma=(0^((n-1)m),c_pi repeated m).

items.name: Maximal multisegment peeling
items.statement: For a type-chi multisegment m, m_max is the multisegment of distinct inclusion-maximal segments, each once; m^max=m-m_max.

api.name: Multisegment.maximalPart_mem
api.statement: A segment occurs in maximalPart(m) iff it occurs in m and no strictly larger segment of m contains it; its multiplicity there is one.

api.name: Multisegment.maximalPart_remainder
api.statement: maximalPart(m)+remainder(m)=m as multisets, with nonnegative multiplicities.

api.name: Multisegment.maximalPart_length_lt
api.statement: If m is nonempty then remainder(m) has strictly smaller total interval length, so repeated peeling terminates.

uses.how: peel one copy of each inclusion-maximal interval.

items.name: Ram additivity for maximal peeling
items.statement: For unipotent/type-chi m, m^ram=(m_max)^ram+(m^max)^ram; no unrestricted additivity is claimed.

items.name: Tuple additivity for maximal peeling
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, lambda_m=lambda_(m_max)+lambda_(m^max), padded to the same rank.

items.name: Weil–Deligne interpretation of ram
items.statement: For unipotent irreducible pi, under the GL_n LLC with geometric Frobenius, pi^ram corresponds to the WD quotient V/(V^I intersect ker N).
items.note: Imports ET.6 full WD/LLC including N. Quotient is not asserted to have no unramified subrepresentation.

items.name: Graded nilpotent pairs
items.statement: A VN-pair is a finite-dimensional Z-graded complex space V with a degree +1 endomorphism N; a WL-pair has a degree -1 operator L. Finite grading support implies nilpotence. Shift V(c)_a=V_(a-c).

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.map
api.statement: A morphism is degree-preserving linear f with fN=N'f; composition preserves that equation.

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.shift_image
api.statement: On an interval VN block [a,b], ImageN(-1) is the truncated interval [a,b-1]; for WL the unshifted ImageL is that interval.

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.nilpotent_of_support
api.statement: If grading support lies in [a,b], either degree-one or degree-minus-one operator has power b-a+1 equal to zero.

uses.how: compute restriction to images and degree shifts.

items.name: Graded pair reconstruction
items.statement: Two VN-pairs are isomorphic iff their underlying graded spaces are isomorphic and their image pairs (Image N,N|Image N) are isomorphic.

items.name: Opposite-degree centralizer spaces
items.statement: For a VN-pair set S(V,N)={degree -1 maps L on V | LN=NL}; for a WL-pair reverse degrees. These are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces with Zariski topology.

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.centralizerSubmodule
api.statement: Degree-minus-one operators commuting with N form a complex linear subspace, hence an irreducible affine space.

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.centralizer_restrict
api.statement: Commutation makes ImageN stable under L; restriction to successive images respects composition of restrictions.

api.name: GradedNilpotentPair.centralizer_generic_intersection
api.statement: A finite intersection of inverse images of nonempty open dense sets under surjective linear restriction maps is nonempty open dense over C.

uses.how: choose opposite operators generically on all relevant images.

items.name: Centralizers restrict surjectively to Image N
items.statement: S(V,N)→S(Image N,N|Image N), by restriction, is surjective.

items.name: Centralizers restrict surjectively to Image L
items.statement: S(W,L)→S(Image L,L|Image L), by restriction, is surjective.

items.name: VN image and segment truncation
items.statement: The VN-pair (Image N(-1),N restricted) corresponds to m^-.

items.name: WL image and segment truncation
items.statement: The WL-pair (Image L,L restricted) corresponds to m^- with NO grading shift.

items.name: Generic commuting operator and duality
items.statement: For a VN-pair of type m there is a dense open S^o(V,N) in S(V,N) whose operators L have WL type m#; the analogous opposite construction holds. One can choose L so that N is generic on (V,L) and on (Image L,L|Image L).
items.note: Split dense-open duality theorem from simultaneous-genericity proof in the next completion pass; cited-input proofs not yet fully audited.

items.name: Ranks compute derivative conductors
items.statement: For unipotent m represented by (V,N), choose commuting L whose restrictions to every Image N^i are in the required generic opens. Then c_(Z(m)^(i))=rank(L N^i), and the rank differences produce the terminal-one formula for lambda.

items.name: Ram and right truncation commute
items.statement: For unipotent/type-chi m, (m^-)^ram=(m^ram)^-.

items.name: Maximal peeling commutes with truncation
items.statement: For type-chi m, (m^-)_max=(m_max)^- and (m^-)^max=(m^max)^-, after discarding empty intervals.

items.name: Weighted inclusion chains and grid paths
items.statement: For integral type-chi m and integer a, take its full submultisegment m_a of intervals INTERSECTING [a,a+1]; E_a is the largest cardinality of a full submultisegment totally ordered by inclusion. Multiplicity counts in cardinality. The grid paths in the proof move (-1,0) or (0,1) from (a+1,a) to (1,r), after translating support to [1,r].

api.name: Multisegment.fullSub_mem
api.statement: A full submultisegment includes either every copy of a distinct interval or none of them.

api.name: Multisegment.chainWeight
api.statement: The weight of a chain of distinct intervals is the sum of their multiplicities in m_a.

api.name: Multisegment.chain_extend_path
api.statement: Every inclusion chain meeting [a,a+1] is contained in the interval set visited by an allowed grid path; maximizing path weight equals maximizing full-chain cardinality.

uses.how: retain all equal copies and maximize weighted chains.

items.name: Adjacent dual interval count
items.statement: For m of type chi and integer a, the number of segments of m# containing [a,a+1] is Card(m_a)-E_a(m), with full multiplicities.

items.name: Finite-DVR-module classes and sorted sequences
items.statement: For a DVR o, C_n consists of finite-length modules generated by at most n elements, up to o-linear isomorphism. seq_n([M]) is the unique ascending nonnegative n-tuple with M≅⊕ o/p^lambda_i. Embed C_n in C_(n+1) by left zero-padding.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.seq_iso
api.statement: Finite-length modules have equal equally padded sequences iff they are isomorphic over o.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.seq_padding
api.statement: seq_(n+1)(M)=(0,seq_n(M)) for M generated by at most n elements.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.layerRank
api.statement: dim_k(p^(j-1)M/p^jM) equals the number of sequence entries at least j, for j>=1.

uses.how: recover invariants without choosing a decomposition.

items.name: Padded additive monoid and lex order on classes
items.statement: Order finite-length DVR-module classes by lex order on equally padded sequences. Define [M] vee [N] by componentwise addition of equally padded sequences.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.vee_seq
api.statement: The sequence of A vee B is the componentwise sum of sequences padded to the same length.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.vee_assoc_comm
api.statement: Vee is associative and commutative with zero-module identity, and is independent of common padding.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.vee_strictMono
api.statement: If A<B and C<=D in padded lex order, then A vee C<B vee D.

uses.how: use ordered additive invariant sequences.

items.name: Monotonicity of vee
items.statement: If [M]<=[N] and [M']<=[N'], then [M]vee[M']<=[N]vee[N']; equality holds only when both original inequalities are equalities.

items.name: Finite-length DVR dual
items.statement: For fraction field F of o, M^vee=Hom_o(M,F/o). This is contravariant, exact on finite-length modules, and noncanonically isomorphic to M.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.dual_map
api.statement: For f:M→N, dual(f):Hom(N,F/o)→Hom(M,F/o) is precomposition; it reverses composition.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.dual_exact
api.statement: A short exact finite-length sequence dualizes to a short exact sequence with arrows reversed, using injectivity of F/o.

api.name: FiniteLengthDVR.dual_cyclic
api.statement: Hom(o/p^a,F/o) is p^-a o/o by evaluation at1; choosing a uniformizer identifies it noncanonically with o/p^a.

uses.how: turn injections into surjections and reverse flags.

items.name: Submodule class inequality
items.statement: An injection of finite-length DVR modules M→M' implies [M]<=[M'].

items.name: Quotient class inequality
items.statement: A surjection of finite-length DVR modules M→M' implies [M]>=[M'].

items.name: DVR convexity
items.statement: For a short exact sequence 0→M'→M→M''→0 of finite-length DVR modules, [M]>=[M']vee[M''].

items.name: Ideal-multiple equality
items.statement: For finite-length M and nonzero ideal I of o, [M]=[IM]vee[M/IM].

items.name: Unique equality-case submodule
items.statement: If [M]=[A]vee[B], there exists exactly one ACTUAL submodule N≤M with [N]=[A] and [M/N]=[B].

items.name: Strict deficit away from equality submodule
items.statement: For that unique N and any other N'≤M, either [N']<[A] or [M/N']<[B].

items.name: Unique equality-case filtration
items.statement: If [M]=[M_1]vee...vee[M_r], there is exactly one ordered filtration 0=F_0≤...≤F_r=M whose graded quotient classes are [M_i].

items.name: Alternative filtration has a deficit
items.statement: Under the preceding equality, every different ordered filtration has some i with [Gr_i F]<[M_i].

items.name: Simultaneous quotient and surjection lifting
items.statement: For surjective f:M→N and submodule M'≤M, the map M→N ×_(N/f(M')) (M/M') is surjective.

items.name: Equal-rank free covers are equivalent
items.statement: For a commutative local ring o, an o-module N, and surjections f:L→N and fprime:Lprime→N from finite free modules of the same rank, there is an o-linear isomorphism alpha:L→Lprime with fprime alpha=f. The source needs the DVR finite-length specialization.
items.note: The direct local-ring proof below avoids the separate projective-cover citation. Its matrix and residue-field adapters remain planning work.

items.name: Ordered generators lift to a basis
items.statement: Given n generators x_i of finite-length N and a surjection f:L→N from a free rank-n module, there is a basis e_i of L with f(e_i)=x_i.

items.name: Admissible filtrations and compatible generators
items.statement: For n=(n_1,...,n_r), n_i>=0 and sum n_i=n, an n-admissible filtration of M has endpoints0,M and each Gr_i generated by at most n_i elements. Ordered n generators are compatible when each prefix of length b_i=sum_(j<=i)n_j spans F_i.

api.name: DVRFiltration.admissible_iff
api.statement: F has endpoints0,M and each F_i/F_(i-1) can be generated by at most n_i elements.

api.name: DVRFiltration.compatible_prefix
api.statement: An ordered list of sum n_i generators is compatible iff its first b_i=sum_(j<=i)n_j entries span F_i.

api.name: DVRFiltration.transport
api.statement: A module isomorphism sends every submodule in F to an admissible filtration with the same quotient generator bounds; transports compose.

uses.how: transport actual filtrations and prescribed quotient bases.

items.name: Image of a free admissible flag
items.statement: For a free rank-n L surjecting onto finite-length M, an n-admissible filtration of L maps to one of M.

items.name: Compatible basis for a free flag
items.statement: Given an n-admissible flag of free rank-n L, a surjection L→M, and any compatible ordered generators x_1,...,x_n of the image flag, there are compatible generators y_1,...,y_n of L lifting the x_i (necessarily a basis since rank L=n).

items.name: Prescribed compatible generators lift through a free flag
items.statement: Given a free admissible flag and compatible generators of its image in M, there is a compatible basis lifting those generators, with the prescribed graded lifts of Lemma4.12(3).

items.name: Exact-generator filtration counts are symmetric
items.statement: For finite-length M over o with FINITE residue field, the number of ordered filtrations whose successive quotients have exactly m_1,...,m_r minimal generators is invariant under permutation of the m_i.

items.name: Lattice-pair stabilizer
items.statement: For full o-lattices L_2⊆L_1⊆F^n, K_(L1,L2) stabilizes both and acts trivially on L_1/L_2. K_(n,[M]) denotes its conjugacy class, not a canonical subgroup.

api.name: Newform.latticeLevel_mem
api.statement: g preserves L1,L2 and induces identity on L1/L2 iff gL1=L1 and (g-1)L1 is contained in L2.

api.name: Newform.latticeLevel_conj
api.statement: For h in GL_n(F), h K_(L1,L2) h^-1=K_(hL1,hL2).

api.name: Newform.latticeLevel_diagonal
api.statement: For L1=o^n and L2=sum p^lambda_i e_i, this stabilizer is the row-depth K_n,lambda.

uses.how: replace matrix levels by quotient lattices.

items.name: Conjugacy depends only on quotient
items.statement: The conjugacy class of K_(L1,L2) depends only on n and the isomorphism class [L1/L2].

items.name: Cosets as lattices with quotient maps
items.statement: For fixed finite-length M generated by <=n elements and a standard quotient o^n→M, G_n/K_(n,[M]) is G_n-equivariantly in bijection with pairs (L,f) of full lattice and surjection f:L→M.

items.name: Flags from parabolic cosets
items.statement: For the partition n=(n_1,...,n_r), G_n/P_n identifies with flags of F-subspaces of prefix dimensions b_i; intersecting such a flag with a lattice identifies it with n-admissible lattice filtrations.

items.name: Double cosets as actual quotient filtrations
items.statement: P_n\G_n/K_(n,[M]) is in bijection with actual n-admissible filtrations of M. In each Mackey summand, projection of P_n∩gKg^-1 to the Levi is the product of the corresponding smaller level groups, up to conjugacy.

items.name: Fixed vectors indexed by module filtrations
items.statement: For finite-length smooth complex pi_i of G_(n_i), n_i>=1 and sum n_i=n, (pi_1×...×pi_r)^(K_(n,[M])) is isomorphic to the direct sum over actual n-admissible filtrations F of M of ⊗_i pi_i^(K_(n_i,[Gr_i F])).

items.name: Reduction to unipotent and L=1 cases
items.statement: Proving both main theorems for every type-chi irreducible with chi unramified, and for every irreducible with L(s,pi)=1, proves them for all Irr(G_n), via the irreducible cuspidal-support factorization of §5.2, tuple/conductor additivity and Proposition5.2.

items.name: Bounded and exact filtration counts
items.statement: N_n(M) is the finite number of n-admissible filtrations of finite-length M, for a nonnegative capacity vector n. Negative capacities give zero; zero capacities are allowed. Exact-generator counts impose equality of generator numbers instead.

api.name: DVRFiltration.count_iso
api.statement: An o-module isomorphism induces a bijection of admissible filtrations and preserves the finite count.

api.name: DVRFiltration.count_zero_capacity
api.statement: Deleting a zero capacity and its forced repeated submodule leaves the count unchanged.

api.name: DVRFiltration.count_exact_sum
api.statement: N_(n1,...,nr)(M) is the sum of exact-generator counts over all 0<=m_i<=n_i.

uses.how: count actual intermediate submodules.

items.name: Ladder determinantal character formula
items.statement: In the Grothendieck group, Z([x_i,y_i]_(i=1..t)) for a type-chi ladder equals sum_(w in S_t) sgn(w) ⊗ind_i Z([x_w(i),y_i]_chi), with empty intervals giving G_0 and negative lengths giving zero.

items.name: Ladder invariant dimensions as alternating counts
items.statement: For that ladder pi of rank n and [M]∈C_n, dim pi^(K_(n,[M]))=sum_(w∈S_t) sgn(w) N_(y_i-x_w(i)+1)_i(M).

items.name: Subquotient generator bound at ladder level
items.statement: Put b=max_(2<=i<=t) max(y_i-x_(i-1)+2,0). If [M]<=[M_pi], then every graded quotient of every filtration of M is generated by at most b elements.

items.name: Five permutation subsets for ladder cancellation
items.statement: Choose a with y_a-x_(a-1)+2=b>0. X1={w | w(k)>=a-1 for k>=a}; X2={w∈X1 | w(k)>=a for k>a}; S={w | w(k)>=a for k>=a}; X3={(a-1,w(a))w | w∈S}; X4={w | w(a)=a-1 and some k>a has w(k)<a-1}; X5={w(a,i(w)) | w∈X4}, with i(w) attaining the largest value among w(1),...,w(a-1).

api.name: LadderCancellation.first_pair
api.statement: On S_t minus X1, swap the positions of the two largest values among w(1),...,w(a-1).

api.name: LadderCancellation.second_pair
api.statement: On X1 minus X2, swap position a with the unique earlier position having value at least a.

api.name: LadderCancellation.remaining_partition
api.statement: X2 is the disjoint union of the block-preserving subgroup S and X3; X3 disjoint-union X4 is {w:w(a)=a-1}.

uses.how: separate disjoint subsets before pairing signs.

items.name: First sign-reversing cancellation
items.statement: For [M]<=[M_pi], swapping the positions of the two largest values among w(1),...,w(a-1) defines a count-preserving sign-reversing involution on S_t\X1, so its signed sum is zero.

items.name: Second sign-reversing cancellation
items.statement: On X1\X2, swapping a with the unique position i<a having w(i)>=a defines a count-preserving sign-reversing involution and its signed sum is zero.

items.name: Remaining subset partition
items.statement: X2 is the disjoint union of S and X3.

items.name: X4 partition and stability
items.statement: X4⊆S_t\X1 is stable under the first involution, and X3 disjoint-union X4={w | w(a)=a-1}.

items.name: X5 stability
items.statement: X5⊆S_t\X1 is stable under the first involution.

items.name: Ladder fixed-space recurrence
items.statement: For [M]<=[M_pi] and b>0 as above, replace the two adjacent segments at a-1,a by [x_a,y_(a-1)] to form pi'. Then dim pi^(K_(n,[M]))=sum_(N≤M, minimalGenerators N=b) dim pi'^(K_(n',[M/N])).

items.name: Newforms for type-chi ladders
items.statement: Theorem2.1 holds for every type-chi ladder; for b=0 use spherical invariants, and for b>0 use the recurrence and unique equality filtration.

items.name: Distinguished constituent multiplicity one
items.statement: Z(m1+m2) occurs with multiplicity one as a subquotient of Z(m1)×Z(m2).

items.name: Truncated constituent criterion
items.statement: For type-chi multisegments, if Z(m) occurs in Z(m1)×Z(m2), then Z(m^-) occurs in Z(m1^-)×Z(m2^-) iff Card(m)=Card(m1)+Card(m2). This is the degree-one form actually used in §6.3.
items.note: Printed lemma allows general multisegments; the c-th-derivative proof needs degree-weighted orders off a degree-one line. General extension remains a gap; see sourceIssues. The source proof uses the ordinary derivative of order Card(m); for general cuspidal degree this must be replaced by the sum of cuspidal degrees. The type-chi application has degree1 throughout.

items.name: Newforms for arbitrary type-chi irreducibles
items.statement: For chi unramified and pi=Z(m) of type chi, Theorem2.1 holds. Induct on (total segment length,number of linked pairs), use maximal peeling and compare all other constituents' tuples strictly.

items.name: Weighted polynomial counting functional
items.statement: Let R=Z[x_1,x_2,...], deg x_i=i, y_m=1+x_1+...+x_m. Define the Z-LINEAR functional xi_M on monomials by the exact-generator filtration count for their index multiset; xi_M(1)=1 if M=0 and0 otherwise.

api.name: DVRFiltration.countLinear_monomial
api.statement: xi_M(product x_(m_i)) is the exact-generator count with capacities m_i>0, independent of ordering by Lemma4.13.

api.name: DVRFiltration.countLinear_add
api.statement: xi_M is Z-linear on MvPolynomial positiveNaturals Z, without any multiplicativity assertion.

api.name: DVRFiltration.countLinear_y
api.statement: xi_M(product_i(1+sum_(j=1)^n_i x_j)) equals the bounded admissible-filtration count.

uses.how: turn the Steinberg alternating sum into a weighted-degree obstruction.

items.name: Bounded counts from y-polynomials
items.statement: xi_M(y_(m1)...y_(ms)) equals the number of (m1,...,ms)-admissible filtrations.

items.name: Degree vanishing from module length
items.statement: If length_o(M)<m, then xi_M(I_m)=0.

items.name: Steinberg composition polynomial bound
items.statement: For n>=1, f_n=sum_(0=n0<...<nr=n) (-1)^(n-r) y_(n1-n0)...y_(nr-n(r-1)) belongs to I_(n-1). The generating-series equality must use the infinite denominator or equality modulo t^(n+1).
items.note: Corrects the finite/infinite series misprint; see sourceIssues.

items.name: Weight vanishing on type-chi lines
items.statement: For unramified chi and pi=Z(m) of type chi, weight(lambda)<c_pi implies pi^(K_n,lambda)=0; reduce to unramified Steinberg constituents and apply the weighted polynomial bound.

items.name: Congruence semigroup and nonunit Hecke ideal
items.statement: X_lambda consists of integral n×n matrices with row i congruent to identity modulo p^lambda_i. H_lambda is the K_n,lambda-biinvariant Hecke subalgebra supported on X_lambda∩G_n; a_lambda is supported on its nonunits, i.e. outside K_n,lambda. Write their images on finite-dimensional V^K with a subscript V.

api.name: Newform.heckeNonunit_mul
api.statement: The product of r nonunits of X_lambda has determinant valuation at least r.

api.name: Newform.heckeUnit
api.statement: With vol(K_n,lambda)=1, the characteristic function of K is the convolution identity on K-biinvariant compactly supported functions.

api.name: Newform.heckeNonunit_ideal
api.statement: Functions supported on the nonunits form a two-sided ideal because determinant valuations of integral matrices are nonnegative.

uses.how: track determinant valuation in convolution.

items.name: Correctly qualified cuspidal nilpotence
items.statement: For cuspidal pi and NONZERO lambda, every T in a_(lambda,V) is nilpotent by compact-mod-center matrix coefficient support and support escape. At lambda=0 the standalone statement is false for unramified GL1 characters; in the L(s,pi)=1 application require a separate proof V^GL_n(o)=0.
items.note: Source defect E2. The nonzero-depth repair and zero-depth spherical-cuspidal classification need an explicit proof contract.

items.name: Nonunit ideal annihilates a simple subspace
items.statement: In the L=1 cuspidal application, after the preceding nilpotence qualification, the nonunit ideal lies in the Jacobson radical of the finite-dimensional image algebra and annihilates every simple submodule of V^K.
items.note: Nil-ideal-to-Jacobson inclusion in a noncommutative algebra is a separate unsupplied library adapter.

items.name: Fourier support at column depths
items.statement: For the row-depth semigroup characteristic function used in §7.1 and the trace pairing, the Fourier transform is supported where column j has depth at least -lambda_j, hence determinant valuation is >=-|lambda|.

items.name: Conductor bound for L=1 representations
items.statement: If L(s,pi)=1 and pi^(K_n,lambda)≠0, then |lambda|>=c_pi. Reduce to cuspidal support, use an a_lambda-annihilated vector and GJ functional equation with the Fourier depth estimate.

items.name: L=1 reduction to single segments
items.statement: For pi=Z(Delta_1+...+Delta_r) with L(s,pi)=1, if Theorem2.1 holds for each single-segment Z(Delta_i), it holds for pi; use the unitriangular constituent transition and equality-case filtration.

items.name: Block groups and the row-stabilizer D
items.statement: In G_nm use standard block Levi L=GL_n^m, its upper block unipotent U, full upper unipotent N, shuffled Levi S=GL_m^n, and V={g | each n×n block g_ij-delta_ij I is strictly upper triangular}. D fixes each last block ROW e_(ni) under right multiplication. iota:G_(n-1)m→G_nm inserts a last row/column identity in every block.

api.name: SpehGroups.iota_mul
api.statement: The block insertion map iota is an injective group homomorphism and maps K' into K.

api.name: SpehGroups.d_factor
api.statement: D=V iota(G'), V intersect iota(G')=iota(V'), and V\D identifies with V'\G'.

api.name: SpehGroups.psi_restrict
api.statement: Psi(g)=psi(sum of g_(i,i+1) for n not dividing i); its restrictions to N,V are homomorphisms but Psi on all G is not.

uses.how: specify embeddings and quotients exactly.

items.name: First quotient identification
items.statement: D=V iota(G') and V∩iota(G')=iota(V'); hence V\D≃V'\G'.

items.name: Second quotient identification
items.statement: N∩D=(N∩V)iota(N') and (N∩V)∩iota(N')=iota(N'∩V'); hence (N∩V)\(N∩D)≃(N'∩V')\N'.

items.name: Zelevinsky and Shalika models
items.statement: Psi(g)=psi(sum_(1<=i<nm,n does not divide i) g_(i,i+1)); its restrictions to N and V are characters. W_Ze^psi(sigma) and W_Sh^psi(sigma) are the images of nonzero maps sigma→Ind_N^G Psi and sigma→Ind_V^G Psi, respectively, when their Hom spaces are one-dimensional.

api.name: SpehModel.left_equivariant
api.statement: A model function satisfies W(ug)=Psi(u)W(g) for u in its designated group N or V.

api.name: SpehModel.right_translate
api.statement: Right translation R_hW(g)=W(gh) preserves the model and commutes with its defining left equivariance.

api.name: SpehModel.realization_unique
api.statement: A nonzero one-dimensional equivariant Hom space determines the image realization independently of scaling its functional.

uses.how: work in concrete functional realizations.

items.name: Zelevinsky-model multiplicity one
items.statement: For tempered Speh sigma, dim Hom_G(sigma,Ind_N^G Psi)=1.

items.name: Shalika-model multiplicity one
items.statement: For tempered Speh sigma, dim Hom_G(sigma,Ind_V^G Psi)=1.

items.name: Levi restriction of Zelevinsky functions
items.statement: Restriction to L lies in the tensor product over i=1,...,m of the Whittaker model of pi|.|^((m+1-2i)(n-1)/2).

items.name: Shalika pairing convergence
items.statement: For W1,W2 in W_Sh^psi(sigma), B(W1,W2,s)=integral_(V\D) W1(g) conjugate(W2(g)) |det g|^s dg converges for Re(s)>-1 and admits meromorphic continuation.

items.name: Shalika invariant inner product
items.statement: B(W1,W2,0) is a positive-definite G-invariant Hermitian form; in particular restriction to D is injective.

items.name: Model transition transforms
items.statement: T^psi W(g)=integral_((V∩N)\V) W(ug)Psi(u)^-1 du. The inverse integrates a Shalika function over (N∩V)\(N∩D) with the same inverse character. Measures are the compatible ones of Lapid–Mao.

api.name: SpehTransition.right_translate
api.statement: T(R_hW)=R_h(TW), and the inverse obeys the same identity.

api.name: SpehTransition.inverse
api.statement: For the compatible quotient measures, the N-to-V and V-to-N integrals are mutually inverse on the Speh models.

api.name: SpehTransition.contragredient
api.statement: T^(psi^-1)(tilde W)(g)=T^psi(W)(w_nm transpose(g)^-1 w'_n).

uses.how: change models without losing invariance or measure factors.

items.name: Compact support for both model transforms
items.statement: The Zelevinsky integrand is compactly supported on (V∩N)\V and the Shalika integrand on (N∩V)\(N∩D), for every right translate.

items.name: Two-sided model isomorphism
items.statement: With the compatible measures, the displayed T and inverse give mutually inverse G-equivariant isomorphisms of the two Speh models.

items.name: Compact induction occurs in model restriction
items.statement: Restriction of the Shalika model to D contains c-Ind_V^D Psi; the analogous assertion holds for every intermediate model, including Zelevinsky, under the generic Speh construction of Lapid–Mao.
items.note: Statements, row-vector D convention, and Lemma3.14 checked in the published cited source. Remaining surrounding proof closure recorded as a gap.

items.name: Unequal-rank Zelevinsky integral
items.statement: For W in W_Ze^psi(sigma), W' in W_Ze^(psi^-1)(sigma'), define I_m(s,W,W')=integral_(N'\G') W(iota(g))W'(g)|det g|^(s-m/2) dg initially in an absolute-convergence half-plane.

api.name: SpehIntegral.I_bilinear
api.statement: In a common convergence half-plane, I_m is complex bilinear in the two model functions; rational continuation preserves this.

api.name: SpehIntegral.I_simultaneous_translate
api.statement: I_m(s,R_iota(h)W,R_hW')=abs(det h)^(-(s-m/2))I_m(s,W,W').

api.name: SpehIntegral.I_levi
api.statement: Iwasawa decomposition gives a finite sum of products of I_1(s-m+i,W_i,W'_i), followed by the compact quotient integral, with its modulus factor.

uses.how: normalize integrals and obtain Laurent module stability.

items.name: Levi decomposition of the integral
items.statement: I_m equals the iterated integral over P'\G' and (N'∩L')\L' of W(iota(lg))W'(lg)|det l|^(s-m/2)delta_P'(l)^-1, with the outer factor |det g|^(s-m/2). Interpret the formal identity first under absolute convergence.

items.name: Absolute convergence of Speh I_m
items.statement: For tempered pi,pi' and the indicated model vectors, I_m converges absolutely for Re(s) sufficiently large (bound may depend on the vectors).

items.name: Denominator bound for I_m
items.statement: I_m(s,W,W') divided by product_(i=1..m)L(s-m+i,pi×pi') belongs to C[q^-s,q^s].

items.name: Contragredient model involution
items.statement: Define tilde W(g)=W(w_nm transpose(g)^-1 w'_n), where w_nm is the full antidiagonal permutation and w'_n the antidiagonal m×m block permutation with I_n blocks. Use the primed analogue for W'.

api.name: SpehModel.tilde_target
api.statement: Tilde maps the psi model of sigma to the psi^-1 model of its smooth contragredient.

api.name: SpehModel.tilde_involutive
api.statement: Applying the displayed full and block Weyl transpose-inverse transform twice returns W.

api.name: SpehModel.tilde_translate
api.statement: Tilde(R_hW)=R_(w'_n transpose(h)^-1 w'_n)(tilde W).

uses.how: track the target representation and additive character.

items.name: Functional equation for I_m
items.statement: I_m(m-s,tilde W,tilde W')=omega_pi'(-1)^((n-1)m) product_(i=1..m) gamma(s-m+i,pi×pi',psi) I_m(s,W,W'). Here gamma=epsilon times L(1-s,tilde pi×tilde pi')/L(s,pi×pi').

items.name: Integral test vector equal to one
items.statement: For W' in the partner Zelevinsky model with W'(1)≠0, some W in the first model satisfies I_m(s,W,W')=1 identically.

items.name: GCD polynomial of the integral family
items.statement: The C-span of all I_m is a fractional ideal in C[X,X^-1], X=q^-s, generated by 1/P_m(X) for unique P_m∈C[X] with P_m(0)=1.

api.name: SpehIntegral.gcdPolynomial_spec
api.statement: The integral span equals P_m(X)^-1 C[X,X^-1], with P_m(0)=1.

api.name: SpehIntegral.gcdPolynomial_unique
api.statement: Two normalized polynomials generating the same fractional ideal by reciprocals are equal.

api.name: SpehIntegral.gcdPolynomial_divides
api.statement: P_m(X) divides product_(i=1)^m P_1(q^(m-i)X), and P_1(X)=L(s,pi times pi')^-1 at X=q^-s.

uses.how: express the gcd without overstating its denominator.

items.name: GCD divisibility bound
items.statement: P_m(X) divides product_(i=1..m)P_1(q^(m-i)X). The paper only obtains equality for an unramified partner downstream of §9, not in general.

items.name: Unequal-rank Shalika integral
items.statement: Z_m(s,W,W')=integral_(V'\G') W(iota(g))W'(g)|det g|^(s-m/2) dg, with opposite additive characters on the two Shalika models.

api.name: SpehIntegral.Z_bilinear
api.statement: In a common absolute-convergence region the Shalika integral is bilinear, and continuation preserves bilinearity.

api.name: SpehIntegral.Z_eq_I
api.statement: For W_Sh=T^psi W_Ze and W'_Sh=T^(psi^-1)W'_Ze, Z_m=I_m with the specified quotient measures.

api.name: SpehIntegral.Z_compact_support
api.statement: If the first restricted function has compact support modulo V', the integral is an ordinary convergent integral whenever the second is smooth and the weight continuous.

uses.how: compare models and define the test transform.

items.name: Model compatibility of integrals
items.statement: If W_Sh=T^psi W_Ze and W'_Sh=T^(psi^-1) W'_Ze, then Z_m(s,W_Sh,W'_Sh)=I_m(s,W_Ze,W'_Ze); the contragredient transforms commute with T in the stated conventions.

items.name: Formal spherical test families
items.statement: For an m×(n-1) matrix x of nonzero complex parameters, define W_Ze^0(ulk;x)=delta_P'(l)^(1/2) product_i W^0(l_i; x_i,*), with u∈U', l∈L', k∈K', and W^0 the normalized spherical Whittaker function with inverse psi. Put W_Sh^0=T'W_Ze^0.

api.name: SpehSpherical.formal_eval
api.statement: For g=ulk, evaluate W_Ze^0 by delta_P'(l)^(1/2) times the product of normalized spherical Whittaker functions on its blocks.

api.name: SpehSpherical.formal_rowSymmetry
api.statement: Permuting Satake parameters within each row leaves W_Ze^0 unchanged; arbitrary row permutations need not preserve the function.

api.name: SpehSpherical.formal_commonScale
api.statement: On det valuation d, multiplying every x_ij by z multiplies W_Ze^0 and W_Sh^0 by z^d.

uses.how: distinguish full parameter families from actual Speh vectors.

items.name: Spherical spanning fails at coincident parameters
items.statement: The literal Lemma8.10 statement for all Satake parameter multisets is false in the n=m=2 specialization with parameters(x,x): spherical-collision supplies two independent eigenfunctions, while the stated family has a single member. A replacement theorem must retain confluent/derivative data at collisions; the generic distinct-parameter statement needs its own proof.
items.note: Strengthens the earlier proof-multiplicity finding using the explicit derivative eigenfunction. This is a provisional source finding, not an independent-review verdict.

items.name: Formal-family convergence
items.statement: For W in the Zelevinsky model and every nonzero parameter matrix x, I_m(s,W,W_Ze^0(x)) converges absolutely for Re(s) sufficiently large.

items.name: Formal-family denominator bound
items.statement: Writing q^(-s_ij)=x_ij, divide I_m(s,W,W_Ze^0(x)) by product_(i,j)L(s+s_ij-(m-1)/2,pi); the result lies in C[q^-s,q^s] and is independent of choices of logarithms.

items.name: Formal-family functional equation
items.statement: I_m(m-s,tilde W,W_Ze^0(x^-1))=product_(i,j)gamma(s+s_ij-(m-1)/2,pi,psi) I_m(s,W,W_Ze^0(x)), with the changed additive-character convention understood.

items.name: Formal-family model compatibility
items.statement: For W_Sh=T W_Ze, I_m(s,W_Ze,W_Ze^0(x))=Z_m(s,W_Sh,W_Sh^0(x)).

items.name: Essential test conditions as a solution set
items.statement: Define Ess(pi,m) to be the set of W∈W_Sh^psi(Sp(pi,m)) right iota(K')-invariant such that for all s and all nonzero x_ij, Z_m(s,W,W_Sh^0(x))=product_(i,j)L(s+s_ij-(m-1)/2,pi). Do NOT define a uniquely chosen vector from these conditions: E1 gives a nonzero common kernel for n=m=2.

api.name: SpehEssential.mem_iff
api.statement: W belongs to Ess(pi,m) iff it is right iota(K')-fixed and every formal test integral equals the specified product of L-factors.

api.name: SpehEssential.add_kernel
api.statement: Adding a right-iota(K')-fixed model vector annihilated by every test preserves membership in Ess.

api.name: SpehEssential.sub_mem_kernel
api.statement: The difference of two essential solutions belongs to the common kernel; if one solution exists then Ess is its affine translate by that kernel.

uses.how: encode the inhomogeneous test equations and their common kernel.

items.name: Existence when L=1
items.statement: If L(s,pi)=1, Ess(pi,m) is nonempty: extend the compactly induced function on D supported on V iota(K') with values Psi, then average under right iota(K').

items.name: Closed transform space Pi
items.statement: Pi is the closure inside L²(V'\G';Psi) of smooth functions obtained by the T' integral from smooth N'-equivariant functions, as specified before Lemma9.3.

api.name: SpehSpectrum.mem_closure
api.statement: Pi consists of L2 limits of the stipulated smooth transformed functions, using the ambient quotient norm.

api.name: SpehSpectrum.closed_invariant
api.statement: The closure is a closed right-G'-invariant subspace wherever the defining transform is justified and right translation is unitary.

api.name: SpehSpectrum.zero_blockSizeOne
api.statement: For primed block size1 and m>=2, T' is identity and its left-N'-invariant L2(G') smooth subspace is zero.

uses.how: distinguish a closure in L2 from all model restrictions.

items.name: Separation restricted to Pi remains an obligation
items.statement: The source claims a smooth right-K'-invariant phi in Pi with all formal spherical test integrals zero must vanish. A valid proof must handle measurable multiplicity spaces and the domains of the test integrals; it cannot be extended to all restricted Speh vectors.
items.note: Open proof audit. In the counterexample specialization Pi=0, so this lemma is vacuous rather than the location of the counterexample.

items.name: Noninjectivity of the essential test transform
items.statement: For n=m=2 and any tempered pi on GL2, let u=[[1,varpi^-1],[0,1]]. f=1_(uK')-1_K' is nonzero, right K'-invariant and compactly supported. Lapid–Mao restriction plus right averaging yields nonzero W in the Shalika model restricting to f. Every Z_m(s,W,W_Sh^0(x)) vanishes. Thus whenever Ess(pi,2) is nonempty it is not a singleton.
items.locator: Diagnostic replacing the invalid uniqueness part of Theorem9.1; E1
items.note: Worker argument, not a result attributed to AKY. Independent confirmation required; full proof in report.

items.name: Levi restriction injectivity requires repair
items.statement: The printed Corollary9.4 asserts that a right-iota(K')-invariant W in the Zelevinsky model with W|L=0 vanishes. Its stated proof invokes the failed §9.1 separation of all restricted vectors. Retain as an unresolved target, not an unconditional import.
items.note: (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026) The paper's gap for this case is recorded as E19.

items.name: Speh lex vanishing target
items.statement: For sigma=Sp(pi,m) and lambda<lambda_sigma, sigma^(K_nm,lambda)=0. The paper reduces to generic newforms via a conjugate level and Corollary9.4; a replacement for that separation step is required.

items.name: Speh row-end level
items.statement: K^(a) consists of k∈GL_nm(o) whose row ni is congruent to row ni of 1 modulo p^a for every i=1,...,m. It is conjugate to K_nm,(0^((n-1)m),a^m).

api.name: SpehLevel.mem
api.statement: Every last row in the n-by-n blocks is congruent to the corresponding identity row modulo p^a.

api.name: SpehLevel.conjugate_rowLevel
api.statement: A permutation in GL_nm(o) conjugates K^(a) to K_nm,(0^((n-1)m),a^m).

api.name: SpehLevel.antitone
api.statement: If a<=b then K^(b) is a subgroup of K^(a); each K^(a) contains iota(K').

uses.how: isolate the stronger level condition from the essential test condition.

items.name: Determinant-sliced test integral
items.statement: For d∈Z, Z_(m,d)(W;x) integrates W(iota(g))W_Sh^0(g;x)|det g|^(-m/2) over the part of V'\G' with |det g|=q^-d. Its generating variable is X=q^-s.

api.name: SpehIntegral.slice_scale
api.statement: Z_(m,d)(W;z x)=z^d Z_(m,d)(W;x) for z nonzero.

api.name: SpehIntegral.slice_sum
api.statement: In the convergence region, Z_m(s,W,W^0(x)) is the sum over d of X^d Z_(m,d)(W;x).

api.name: SpehIntegral.slice_reflect

items.name: Uniform lower support bound
items.statement: For every Shalika vector W there exists integer d(W), independent of x, with Z_(m,d)(W;x)=0 for d<d(W). If W_Ze is right V''(p^ell)-invariant one may take d(W)=-(n-1)m ell.

items.name: Level-dependent lower bounds
items.statement: For W fixed by K^(a), one may take d(W)=0 and d(tilde W)=-(n-1)ma in the determinant-slice bound.

items.name: Finite support when L=1
items.statement: If L(s,pi)=1, put d'(W)=-c_pi m(n-1)-d(tilde W). Then Z_m(s,W,W_Sh^0(x))=sum_(d(W)<=d<=d'(W)) X^d Z_(m,d)(W;x).

items.name: Corrected finite Laurent functional equation
items.statement: For L=1, epsilon(s,pi,psi)=epsilon_0 q^(-c_pi s), the sum over tilde-W support of q^(-md)X^(-d) Z_(m,d)(tilde W;x^-1) equals epsilon_0^(m(n-1)) q^(c_pi*m*(m-1)*(n-1)/2) X^(c_pi*m*(n-1)) product_(i,j)x_ij^c_pi times the sum over W support of X^d Z_(m,d)(W;x).

items.name: L=1 Speh newform line target
items.statement: For L(s,pi)=1, the K^(c_pi)-fixed Shalika space is one-dimensional and admits an element satisfying the essential test conditions. The printed claim that an arbitrarily unique essential vector spans it must be replaced; proof currently unclosed.

items.name: General tempered Speh newform line target
items.statement: For tempered pi, dim Sp(pi,m)^(K^(c_pi))=1. This is the source's Corollary9.9 after the reduction chain; do not deduce it from invalid essential uniqueness.

items.name: Restriction of Speh newform line to Levi
items.statement: Conditional on repaired preceding proofs, restriction identifies W_Ze(sigma)^(K^(c_pi)) with the tensor over i of the generic K_(n,(0^(n-1),c_pi))-newform lines for pi|.|^((m+1-2i)(n-1)/2).

items.name: General essential existence target
items.statement: For every tempered pi, Ess(pi,m) is nonempty, constructed by normalized generic essential functions on the Levi and the newform restriction isomorphism. This is an existence claim only; the uniqueness claim is rejected pending independent review of E1.

items.name: Unramified partner GCD equality target
items.statement: When pi' is unramified, the source obtains P_m(X)=product_(i=1..m)P_1(q^(m-i)X) from essential existence. Its analytic proof branch is presently conditional on repaired §9 existence.

items.name: Mirahoric representations
items.statement: Segments are tightly linked when linked and either nonunipotent or with nonempty intersection. L(m) is mirahoric if no pair in m is tightly linked; equivalently c_(pi^highest)=0, equivalently lambda_pi has at most one positive entry.

api.name: Mirahoric.tightlyLinked
api.statement: A linked pair is tightly linked iff it is nonunipotent or its intersection is nonempty.

api.name: Mirahoric.langlands_iff
api.statement: L(m) is mirahoric iff no pair of segments of m is tightly linked.

api.name: Mirahoric.conductorTuple_iff
api.statement: Mirahoric is equivalent to zero conductor of the highest derivative and to a tuple with at most one positive component.

items.name: Nonarchimedean Schwartz–Bruhat Fourier interface
items.statement: Use compactly supported locally constant functions on finite-dimensional F-spaces, trace/additive pairing psi and compatible self-dual Haar measures; Fourier inversion includes reflection.

api.statement: Fourier transforming a translate by a multiplies the transform by the additive pairing with a, with the sign fixed by the chosen kernel.

api.name: LocalFourier.indicator_lattice
api.statement: For an additive lattice L with self-dual measure, Fourier(1_L)=vol(L)1_(L-perp).

api.name: LocalFourier.inversion

items.statement: Import Godement–Jacquet standard factors and JPSS Whittaker Rankin–Selberg factors, with rationality, normalized fractional ideals, functional equations and dependence on psi; gamma(s)=epsilon(s)L(1-s,dual)/L(s).

api.name: LocalFactor.induction_product

items.name: Normalized spherical Whittaker functions
items.statement: For a nonzero Satake multiset, use the normalized K-fixed Whittaker function of the unramified principal-series family. When the parameters have unit modulus, it specializes to the irreducible tempered spherical representation. An arbitrary unramified irreducible constituent can be nongeneric, so it need not itself have a Whittaker model.

api.name: SphericalWhittaker.value_one
api.statement: The normalized K-fixed Whittaker function of the unramified principal-series family has value1 at identity.

api.name: SphericalWhittaker.satake_symmetric
api.statement: Its value depends symmetrically on the nonzero Satake parameters, with the fixed inverse-psi convention.

api.name: SphericalWhittaker.tempered_specialization
api.statement: For unit-modulus Satake parameters it belongs to the Whittaker model of the irreducible tempered spherical representation; arbitrary unramified constituents need not be generic.

items.name: Generic GL_n newform and essential Whittaker inputs
items.statement: For generic irreducible pi of GL_n(F), the K_(n,(0^(n-1),c_pi))-fixed space is one-dimensional, lower conductor levels vanish, and normalized essential Whittaker functions give the classical unramified test integrals. The exact corrected JPSS theorem and normalization must be audited with Jacquet2012 before closure.
items.note: GL2 specialization is already owned by R16.2; general GL_n extension imports and compares it, without replanning the rank-two result.

items.name: Existing GL2 generic newvector theorem
items.statement: For generic irreducible GL2(F) representations, import the local conductor/newvector theorem planned by R16.2 and compare the row-depth (0,c) subgroup with its K1 convention.

items.name: L=1 multisegment tuple
items.statement: For pi=Z(sum Delta_i) with L(s,pi)=1, no Delta_i is unipotent and lambda_pi is the sum of padded tails c_rho_i repeated length(Delta_i); c_rho_i>0.

items.name: Existing weighted multivariate polynomial grading
items.statement: For a commutative semiring R, any variable set sigma and weight w:sigma→M to a decidable additive commutative monoid, MvPolynomial sigma R decomposes into its weighted homogeneous submodules as a graded algebra. Apply to positive natural variables over Z with weight i; no finiteness of the variable set is required.

items.name: Existing Baer extension criterion
items.statement: For a ring R and R-module Q satisfying Module.Baer R Q, every linear map M→Q extends along every injective linear map M→N. In particular Q is injective.

items.name: Existing noncommutative Jacobson membership criterion
items.statement: For any ring R and left ideal I, x belongs to I.jacobson iff for every y there exists z such that z*y*x+z-1 belongs to I. This statement does not assume commutativity.

items.name: Existing geometric inverse for a nilpotent element
items.statement: For any ring R, if r is nilpotent then 1+r is a unit; its inverse is the finite alternating geometric sum through any vanishing power. No commutativity assumption on R is needed.

items.name: Existing surjectivity form of Nakayama
items.statement: For commutative R, an R-linear f:M→N with N finitely generated, and I contained in the Jacobson radical, surjectivity after composing with N→N/IN implies surjectivity of f.

items.name: Intrinsic uniqueness of the finite-DVR sequence
items.statement: For a DVR o with residue field k and finite-length M, put r_j=dim_k(p^(j-1)M/p^jM) for j>=1. In any cyclic decomposition r_j counts the exponents at least j. Hence multiplicity of exponent j is r_j-r_(j+1), the minimal number of generators is r_1, and the unique ascending n-term sequence is obtained by padding with n-r_1 zeros.
items.locator: Section4.1 classification input; continuation proof from cyclic decomposition

items.name: Injectivity of the fraction-field quotient over a PID
items.statement: For a PID o with fraction field F, the o-module F/o is injective. Consequently restriction Hom_o(M,F/o)→Hom_o(N,F/o) is surjective for every injection N→M, without a finite-length hypothesis.
items.locator: Input to Lemma4.3(1); continuation Baer proof

items.name: Exactness and biduality for finite-DVR duals
items.statement: Over a DVR o with fraction field F, Hom_o(-,F/o) is exact contravariantly on finite-length modules; the evaluation M→Hom_o(Hom_o(M,F/o),F/o) is a natural isomorphism. It preserves finite length and cyclic exponents.
items.locator: Lemmas4.2–4.3 and duality use in Proposition4.4; continuation proof

items.name: A second eigenfunction at coincident GL2 parameters
items.statement: In the n=m=2 primed setup, fix x nonzero and write g=n diag(varpi^a,varpi^b)k. Set F(g)=q^(-(a-b)/2)x^(a+b) and H(g)=(a-b)F(g). Both are smooth left-N-invariant right-K-invariant Hecke eigenfunctions with the same Satake character (x,x). They are linearly independent since F(1)=1,H(1)=0,H(diag(varpi,1))=q^-1/2 x. The single formal assignment (x,x) spans only F, refuting the literal Lemma8.10 spanning assertion in this specialization.
items.locator: Published Lemma8.10 p47; arXiv v4 p51; worker continuation argument E3

items.name: Infinite-dimensional common kernel in the rank-two Speh test
items.statement: For n=m=2 and tempered pi on GL2, the common kernel of all essential test integrals on right-iota(Kprime)-fixed Shalika vectors is infinite-dimensional. For r>=1 put u_r=I+varpi^-r E12 and f_r=1_(u_rKprime)-1_Kprime. Every finite collection has linearly independent restrictions, and each has a model lift after right averaging.
items.locator: Theorem9.1 obstruction E1; continuation of essential-kernel

items.name: Uniform escape of nonunits at nonzero row depth
items.statement: Let lambda≠0 and C⊂GL_n(F) be compact. There is B(C,lambda) such that for z central and g∈C with zg∈X_lambda, the determinant valuation v(det(zg))<=B. Thus X_lambda with determinant valuation tending to infinity escapes every compact subset modulo the center.
